answer: Require a memory-hard proof per identity: each answer must fill and traverse a large table sized to one key's seed, binding the work to space, not cycles. One honest worker holds a single atlas of memory once per epoch. A farm needs that whole table resident per fake at the same instant, and finite RAM caps how many comet-brief identities run at once; the lotus of shared precomputation never blooms because each table is seeded uniquely. Sybil scale is throttled by hardware memory, not just CPU.
